newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Switzerland orders freeze on Mobutu's villa.
newsitem.headline: Switzerland orders freeze on Mobutu's villa.

text.p: Switzerland ordered a freeze on Friday on the villa of Zaire's president Mobutu Sese Seko but not other assets of the embattled ruler, estimated to total $4 billion by Swiss media.

"The Federal Justice Department, in accordance with the Foreign Ministry and on the basis of the request for legal assistance on May 7 from the prosecutor in Lubumbashi, has decided to freeze Mobutu's property in Savigny as a preventative measure," a government statement said.

The government statement said the public prosecutor of the Zairean town of Lubumbashi who asked Switzerland to freeze the assets of Mobutu "appears therefore to be a competent representative of the Zairean judicial authorities."

It said the federal police and justice authorities had asked the canton of Vaud to put the villa, valued at more than $2.5 million according to Swiss media, on the real estate register as "blocked" and "cannot be transferred until further notice".

It said the Zairean request did not have sufficient details on other assets Mobutu allegedly had in Switzerland and "for the moment, does not allow the possible adoption of other measures". Switzerland would be asking further information on this issue, it added.

The statement said the Swiss move "does not in any way equal a recognition of a (Zairean rebel leader Laurent) Kabila government." Switzerland's banking watchdog, the Federal Banking Commission, has already ordered an official search for any Mobutu accounts among the country's banks and given them until the end of May to report.
